Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungal infection by Cercospora zeae-maydis, favored by high humidity and warm temperatures.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply fungicides containing strobilurins or triazoles (e.g., Azoxystrobin, Propiconazole) at disease onset.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Use resistant maize hybrids and practice crop rotation.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Fungal pathogen (Puccinia sorghi), spreads via airborne spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Apply Mancozeb or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC foliar spray at the first sign of disease to prevent spread to top leaves.

treatment_severity.Mild: Monitor closely. Apply a prophylactic spray of Mancozeb if conditions are humid.
treatment_severity.Moderate: Apply Mancozeb or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC foliar spray to prevent spread to top leaves.
treatment_severity.Severe: Immediate application of Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC at higher recommended dose. Remove heavily infected lower leaves.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant maize varieties where available. Practice crop rotation with non-host crops like pulses.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungal infection by Exserohilum turcicum, thrives in moderate temperatures and heavy dews.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Foliar fungicide applications (e.g., Mancozeb, Pyraclostrobin) when lesions first appear.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and till residue to reduce overwintering inoculum.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard agricultural practices.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection by Xanthomonas campestris, spread by splashing rain and contaminated seeds.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides combined with Mancozeb to reduce spread.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal infection (Alternaria solani), spreads in warm humid conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g per liter of water. Apply twice at weekly intervals upon noticing disease incidence.

treatment_severity.Mild: Prune lower infected leaves. Apply copper-based fungicide as a preventative measure.
treatment_severity.Moderate: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g per liter of water. Apply twice at weekly intervals.
treatment_severity.Severe: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g per liter immediately. Destroy severely blighted plants to protect remaining crop.

Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops yearly. Ensure adequate spacing between plants for airflow.

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans, rapidly spreads in cool, wet conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply systemic fungicides (e.g., Metalaxyl, Cymoxanil) combined with protectants like Chlorothalonil.

treatment_severity.Mild: Apply contact fungicides (e.g., Chlorothalonil) as soon as mild lesions appear.
treatment_severity.Moderate: Apply systemic fungicides (e.g., Metalaxyl) to control spreading infection.
treatment_severity.Severe: Immediate systemic fungicide application. Rogue and destroy severely infected plants immediately.

Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Eliminate cull piles, control volunteer plants, and ensure good field drainage.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungal infection by Passalora fulva, primarily an issue in high-humidity environments like greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply fungicides such as Chlorothalonil or Copper fungicides at the first sign of symptoms.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Ensure adequate ventilation and spacing to lower humidity around plants.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungal infection by Septoria lycopersici, spores spread via rain splash or overhead irrigation.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Spray with protectant fungicides like Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb on a 7-10 day schedule.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch around the base of plants and remove infected lower leaves to prevent splash spread.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Infestation by Tetranychus urticae, often exacerbated by hot, dry conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Apply specific miticides (e.g., Abamectin, Spiromesifen) or insecticidal soaps. Ensure coverage on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Maintain adequate plant hydration and use predatory mites (e.g., Phytoseiulus persimilis) as biocontrol.

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Fungal infection by Corynespora cassiicola, favored by high humidity and prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply targeted systemic fungicides such as Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Avoid working in fields when plants are wet and ensure good canopy airflow.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Viral infection caused by TYLCV, transmitted primarily by the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no cure for the virus. Treatment focuses on vector control: apply systemic insecticides (e.g., Imidacloprid) to manage whitefly populations.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Plant resistant tomato varieties, use reflective mulches, and apply fine-mesh netting.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Viral infection by ToMV, highly contagious and spread through mechanical contact, contaminated tools, or seeds.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No chemical treatment available. Infected plants must be immediately uprooted and destroyed.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Disinfect tools with bleach, wash hands frequently, and use certified virus-free seeds.

Tomato___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard agricultural practices.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Fungal infection by Guignardia bidwellii, requires wet leaves to infect.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply protectant fungicides like Mancozeb or systemic options like Myclobutanil during early growth stages.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out infected canes, destroy mummified berries, and maintain an open canopy.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Complex of fungal pathogens (including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora) infecting the vascular tissue.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No effective chemical cure. Some mitigation through trunk renewal or applying wound protectants post-pruning.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid pruning during wet weather and apply pruning wound sealants to prevent spore entry.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Fungal infection by Pseudocercospora vitis, thrives in late summer during warm, humid periods.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or broad-spectrum fungicides such as Mancozeb upon early detection.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Remove fallen debris and optimize trellising for maximum air circulation.

Grape___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard agricultural practices.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.

Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply appropriate contact or systemic fungicide (e.g., Mancozeb). Consult local agricultural extension officer.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers. Implement crop rotation.

Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply appropriate contact or systemic fungicide (e.g., Mancozeb). Consult local agricultural extension officer.

treatment_severity.Mild: Apply contact fungicides like Mancozeb at first sign of symptoms.
treatment_severity.Moderate: Apply systemic fungicides (e.g., Metalaxyl-M) combined with a protectant.
treatment_severity.Severe: Immediate aggressive systemic spraying. Destroy heavily infected foliage to protect tubers.

Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers. Implement crop rotation.

Potato___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard agricultural practices.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.
